svg.title: Alpha-beta cutoffs in a real position
svg.desc: A two-ply search for Black in the test midgame position. Each row is a black move with the evaluated white replies. a3 is searched fully and gives alpha -105. For f3 the reply b4 = -124 is below alpha, so four replies are skipped. c6 gives 61, the new best. For a4 the first reply c1 = 45 is below 61, so eleven replies are skipped.
svg.text: Alpha-beta at depth 2: Black moves, White replies, leaves evaluated for Black
a3 = −105: first move: all replies; alpha = −105
c6 = 61: better: alpha = 61, best move c6
Blue = the lowest reply (White picks it). Red = the reply that proves the move is not better than alpha; the grey replies are never evaluated.
Over all 11 moves, plain minimax evaluates 124 leaves and alpha-beta in this order 45; Stello's depth-2 iteration, with its ordering, 21. Result: c6, 61.
